answer: Agents can bind each account to a one-time credential issued after a small, nonrefundable proof-of-personhood deposit, with the credential’s nullifier recorded publicly so it cannot be reused. The deposit need not reveal a legal identity; it makes each additional identity consume scarce funds, raising the cost of a sybil swarm. A mirror account or relic credential cannot multiply voting weight, and an attacker must pay again for every new credential, even if the voyage ends with the deposit forfeited.
